newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algiers car bomb kills one, wounds 20 - officials.
newsitem.headline: Algiers car bomb kills one, wounds 20 - officials.

text.p: A car bomb exploded on a street near a crowded coffee shop in central Algiers on Monday killing at least one person and wounding 20, Algerian security forces said.
"I saw much blood at the scene. I fear many people might have died," one witness said by telephone from Algiers after the explosion at 12.45 a.m. (1145 GMT)
The statement from Algerian security forces, carried by state-run Algerian radio, said one person had died and 20 were wounded but said the toll was provisional.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the blast. Algerian authorities have blamed a series of bombings on Moslem guerrillas.
More than 1,400 civilians have died in bomb attacks by fundamentalist Moslem rebels in the past two years, according to a government human rights body.
Monday's car bomb ripped through the commercial Larbi Ben Mehidi's street at rush hour, destroying the cafe and damaging a pizzeria and a betting office, withnesses said.
"A young man hurriedly left a car he had just parked near Novelty cafe and a moment later the explosion hit the place," said one man, speaking by telephone from his office near the site of the blast.

Another witness said "trails of blood covered the pavement" and the Novelty cafe was completed wrecked. "There were many people in the place as employees left offices for lunch and a lot of passers-by were also there."
About 60,000 people, mostly Moslem militants and security forces members, have died since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election radical Islamists were set to win.

On January 30, 1995, a suicide car bomb in central Algiers killed at least 42 people and wounded nearly 300. The Armed Islamic Group, the most ruthless of Algeria's fundamentalist guerrilla movements, claimed responsibility.
Last August 1, a remote-controlled bomb killed French Roman Catholic bishop Pierre Claverie at his residence in the western city of Oran, hours after he met French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
Three days later a truck bomb wounded dozens in the central town of Tiaret, 225 km (140 miles) southwest of Algiers.
On August 6, a home-made bomb wounded five people in a restaurant in central Algiers and on August 8 a similar bomb ripped through an Algiers coffee shop, wounding at least seven people.
